rules.rule: If a protected-data host shows a successful sign-in followed by listing of restricted data, isolate it immediately before any file read or exfiltration can occur.
After isolating, confirm containment in logs and processes, report the evidence chain, and verify the actual service inventory before patching or restoring the host.
After restoring a contained host, monitor its logs for new sign-in or restricted-listing evidence and only re-isolate if compromise recurs, to limit downtime.
When isolation blocks a restricted read and subsequent logs show no new alerts, hold containment and wait rather than restoring, to prevent exfiltration despite downtime cost.
Do not divert containment to decoy scans on unrelated hosts when logs already link a successful sign-in and restricted listing on the protected host.
Report early perimeter-probe suspicion promptly, then continue log checks and isolate on confirmed sign-in and restricted-listing evidence without waiting for further reports.
When an intermediate host shows a successful sign-in and access to credential-bearing backups, isolate it promptly and assume harvested credentials will be reused against a downstream host.
Isolating an intermediate host does not block already-harvested credentials, so keep checking downstream hosts and isolate the protected host on sign-in before any restricted read succeeds.
